title: Before Retrieval Begins: Safety and Tool-Use Decisions in LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.23071v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as agents that call external tools, yet most tool-safety research examines only what follows a tool call. The prior decision of whether to call the tool remains largely unexamined and can influence downstream safety. Across the seven open-weight models, the unweighted model-average harm rate after admitted harmful requests is 74.5%. To identify what governs this decision, we apply a factorial intervention to the input request. Within our generated construction, neutralizing the requested-operation component produces the largest admission contrast (19 pp). A linear direction estimated from this contrast influences held-out admission in four of seven models; effects on operation-neutralized requests in some models show that it is not an operation-specific mechanism. We then test whether written refusal is behaviorally and representationally coupled to the same decision. Written refusal accompanies 33.

translated_title: 检索开始之前：大语言模型智能体的安全与工具使用决策
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型越来越多地充当调用外部工具的智能体，然而大多数工具安全研究只考察工具调用之后发生的事情。是否调用工具这一前置决策在很大程度上未被研究，却可能影响下游的安全性。在七个开放权重模型中，有害请求被接受后的未加权模型平均有害率为74.5%。为了确定是什么因素支配这一决策，我们对输入请求施加了因子化干预。在我们构建的生成数据中，将“请求操作”组件中和后产生了最大的接受率对比（19个百分点）。从该对比中估计出的线性方向影响了七个模型中四个模型在保留集上的接受行为；而该方向在某些模型中对操作已被中和的请求仍有效应，说明它并非特定于某种操作的机制。随后我们检验了书面拒绝在行为层面和表征层面是否与同一决策相耦合。书面拒绝伴随着33.（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文首次系统研究了大语言模型智能体在工具调用发生之前“是否调用工具”这一前置安全决策，发现有害请求被接受后的平均有害率高达74.5%，并通过因子化干预揭示“请求操作”组件是支配该决策的关键因素，同时发现书面拒绝在行为与表征上与该决策相互耦合。
en_tdlr: This paper is the first to systematically examine LLM agents' pre-retrieval decision of whether to call a tool, revealing a 74.5% average harm rate after admitted harmful requests, identifying the requested-operation component as the key governing factor via factorial interventions, and showing that written refusal is behaviorally and representationally coupled to this same decision.
